Sep 21, 2026, 10:38 PM ET
Across 572 plate appearances in 2026, Arizona Diamondbacks third baseman Nolan Arenado is hitting .247/.322/.455 with 27 home runs, 78 RBI, 73 runs scored, and four stolen bases. After hitting just 28 home runs across over 1,000 plate appearances in his final two seasons with the St. Louis Cardinals in 2024 and 2025, it's been a resurgent campaign for the 35-year-old. Arenado has also been red-hot of late, hitting .317 with six home runs and 13 RBI across 68 plate appearances in September. Arenado also has a favorable schedule in the final week of the regular season, as the Diamondbacks will open a three-game set at Coors Field against the Colorado Rockies on Tuesday. In any league where he is available on the waiver wire, Arenado profiles as a priority target for fantasy managers.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
More Recent News
Sep 21, 2026, 10:59 PM ET
Across 348 plate appearances since making his MLB debut in early June, Colorado Rockies outfielder/shortstop Cole Carrigg is hitting .271/.335/.461 with 10 home runs, 48 RBI, 46 runs scored, and 11 stolen bases. The 24-year-old has been a balanced producer for fantasy managers for most of the second half of the season. However, he's been particularly hot in recent weeks. Across 77 plate appearances in September, Carrigg is hitting .307 with four home runs, 12 RBI, eight runs scored, and three stolen bases. Carrigg also has a favorable schedule to end the year, with three games at home against the Arizona Diamondbacks followed by three games in Chicago against the White Sox. In leagues where he remains available on the waiver wire, Carrigg profiles as an outfield streamer for fantasy managers to target.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Sep 21, 2026, 10:47 PM ET
Across 431 plate appearances in 2026, Texas Rangers third baseman Josh Jung is hitting .295/.360/.450 with 11 home runs, 39 RBI, 52 runs scored, and one stolen base. After suffering a calf injury in late July, Jung missed almost two months' worth of action. However, the 28-year-old has hit well since returning to the Rangers lineup on September 12. Across his last 35 plate appearances, Jung is hitting .303 with two home runs, four RBI, and six runs scored. Jung has posted a career-best 48.7% hard-hit rate in 2026 while also dropping his strikeout rate to a career-low 18.1%. In fantasy leagues where he's not already rostered, Jung could be worth targeting on the waiver wire for the final week of the 2026 season.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Robert Suarez Expected to Return This Week


Will Brady




Sep 21, 2026, 10:29 PM ET
Atlanta Braves general manager Alex Anthopoulos said during a radio appearance on 680 The Fan that right-hander Robert Suarez (elbow) is "highly likely" to be activated from the 60-day injured list on either Wednesday or Thursday. Suarez has been sidelined since mid-June by inflammation in his right elbow, but it appears he will be back in the Atlanta bullpen for the team's postseason push. Across 32 innings (31 games) before suffering the injury, Suarez recorded a 0.56 ERA, 0.84 WHIP, 26 strikeouts, and four saves. While the 35-year-old's strikeout rate dropped to 21.5%, he allowed just one home run (0.28 HR/9). Upon his return, Suarez should be a key part of the bridge to Braves closer Raisel Iglesias.--Will Brady
Source: 680 The Fan
Sep 21, 2026, 10:20 PM ET
San Francisco Giants outfielder Jung Hoo Lee (groin) has been placed on the 10-day injured list with a groin contusion, per Justice delos Santos of The Mercury News. With less than 10 days remaining in the regular season, Lee's 2026 campaign is over. Across 579 plate appearances for the year, Lee hit .276/.320/.404 with 10 home runs, 57 RBI, 65 runs scored, and 12 stolen bases. The 28-year-old has a firm ceiling on his power, as he owns just a 3.1% barrel rate and a 33% hard-hit rate for his career. However, Lee struck out in fewer than 10% of his plate appearances this season and should continue to provide fantasy managers with a solid batting average and run production in 2027. With Lee sidelined, Giants outfielder Bo Davidson could take over as the team's everyday right fielder.--Will Brady
Source: The Mercury News - Justice delos Santos
Willy Adames Returns to Baseball Activities


Will Brady




Sep 21, 2026, 10:12 PM ET
San Francisco Giants shortstop Willy Adames (elbow) fielded ground balls and took batting practice on Monday, per Justice delos Santos of The Mercury News. Adames has been sidelined since late August by an elbow injury and is unlikely to play again in 2026. However, the 31-year-old appears to be making progress and should have a relatively normal offseason heading into 2027. Across 505 plate appearances in 2026, Adames hit .230/.289/.424 with 21 home runs, 51 RBI, 62 runs scored, and six stolen bases. The veteran shortstop's barrel (8.9%) and hard-hit (38.8%) rates were both his worst since the 2019 season. Adames also graded out as one of the worst defensive shortstops in MLB, which is usually one of the strengths of his game. If the elbow injury was impacting his performance before he was finally placed on the injured list, Adames could be a worthy buy-low target for fantasy managers in 2027.--Will Brady
Source: The Mercury News - Justice delos Santos
Bryce Eldridge Finishes Year on Concussion Injured List


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 7:24 PM ET
The San Francisco Giants placed rookie first baseman Bryce Eldridge (concussion) on the seven-day concussion injured list on Monday, ending his first full season with just a week left to play, according to Justice delos Santos of The San Jose Mercury News. The 21-year-old left-handed slugger had a cup of coffee with San Fran in 2025, playing in only 10 games, but he finishes 2026 with 107 games played at the major-league level. In those 107 games (448 plate appearances), Eldridge showed plenty of power potential at Oracle Park, slashing .269/.364/.461 with an .825 OPS, 17 homers, 57 RBI, 50 runs scored, and one stolen base. It was a disappointing end to the year, though, as he suffered a concussion when he hit his head at the team's hotel. The former first-rounder also hit .333 (38-for-114) with five homers and 22 RBI in 30 games at Triple-A Sacramento in 2026. One of the Giants' top prospects, outfielder Bo Davidson, and infielder Marcelo Mayer will get a chance to impress over the final week of the regular season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The San Jose Mercury News - Justice delos Santos
Troy Melton Lands on Injured List With Arm Fatigue


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 7:08 PM ET
The Detroit Tigers announced on Monday that they placed right-hander Troy Melton (forearm) on the 15-day injured list with right-arm fatigue and recalled right-handed pitching prospect River Ryan from Triple-A Toledo in a corresponding move. Melton felt something in his right forearm during his final outing of the season on Sunday in an 8-1 loss to the division-rival Chicago White Sox, allowing four earned runs on four hits while walking three and striking out four in 3 2/3 innings to pick up his fifth loss of the year. The 25-year-old former fourth-round pick in 2022 from San Diego State University had a strong second season in the majors altogether, going 8-5 with a 2.76 ERA (4.09 FIP) and 1.13 WHIP with 94 strikeouts and 37 walks in 114 1/3 innings across his 20 starts. Melton produced an identical 2.76 ERA in his MLB debut in 2025, too, in 16 appearances (four starts) covering 45 2/3 frames. A deep pitch mix with strong command makes Melton an intriguing and ascending young arm for fantasy managers going into the 2027 season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Tigers PR
Giants Calling Up Outfield Prospect Bo Davidson


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 6:52 PM ET
The San Francisco Giants are calling up outfield prospect Bo Davidson, the team's No. 8 prospect per MLB Pipeline, to the big leagues on Monday, a source told Justice delos Santos of The San Jose Mercury News. Davidson will get the call to the big leagues to begin the final week of the 2026 regular season after hitting .309/.389/.534 with 10 home runs and six steals for Triple-A Sacramento this year in 52 games across 234 plate appearances. He also hit .277/.340/.521 with an .861 OPS, 19 homers, 53 RBI, 14 steals, and 49 runs scored in 73 games and 315 plate appearances at Double-A Richmond. Obviously, it is too late in the season for Davidson to do any real damage in fantasy baseball leagues, but the Gigantes will get a look at one of their best position-player prospects in the final week, with both outfielder Jung Hoo Lee (groin) and Bryce Eldridge (head) currently dealing with injuries. The 24-year-old left-handed hitter has primarily played center field in the minors, but he could be used in a corner-outfield spot as well. Davidson has intriguing raw power from the left side and could push for an early MLB return in 2027 if he starts out hot in the minors.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The San Jose Mercury News - Justice delos Santos
Dylan Cease Will Not Need Shoulder Surgery


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 5:58 PM ET
Toronto Blue Jays right-hander Dylan Cease (shoulder) said he will not need surgery on his right shoulder following his MRI results, according to Hazel Mae of Sportsnet. Cease is now in "limbo" on what his next steps are, depending on where the team is in the American League playoff picture. The talented right-hander described his shoulder feeling as a "bit heavy and achy and not normal. But at the same time, it didn't feel like it was torn... not something I need surgery for or anything like that. It was just inflammation, just the kind of that middle ground." Toronto heads into Monday's series opener on the road against the division-rival Baltimore Orioles three games back of the final wild-card spot in the AL with six games left to play. If the Jays are still alive by the weekend, Cease could make his final start of the 2026 season at home against the Cincinnati Reds. The 30-year-old has had a banner year in Toronto in his first year with the club, going 11-6 with a 2.40 ERA, league-leading 2.55 FIP, a 1.10 WHIP, a career-high 239 strikeouts, and 78 walks in 169 innings and 29 starts.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Sportsnet - Hazel Mae
Sep 21, 2026, 5:52 PM ET
Chicago Cubs star third baseman Alex Bregman (face) suffered multiple facial fractures after being hit by a foul ball while standing in the on-deck circle on Sunday, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan. Bregman will not undergo surgery and is hopeful to return for the postseason in October. It was a scary moment, but thankfully, the 32-year-old veteran is alright and should return to help the Cubbies for their playoff run next month. The three-time All-Star will finish his first year in Chitown with a .262/.352/.452 slash line, an .804 OPS, 26 home runs, 89 RBI, 89 runs scored, and three stolen bases in 153 games played across 693 plate appearances in his 11th year in the big leagues. It was a bounce-back season after he played in only 114 games a year ago in his lone season with the Boston Red Sox. Bregman hit .296 (34-for-115) with 12 home runs and 30 RBI in 28 games in August and was hitting .295 (18-for-61) with three homers in 18 games in September, so Chicago will be hoping that he does not miss a beat at the plate when he hopefully returns for the start of the wild-card series next week.--Keith Hernandez
Source: ESPN.com - Jeff Passan
Sep 21, 2026, 4:21 PM ET
Baltimore Orioles middle infielder Jackson Holliday (wrist) is unlikely to play for the Orioles again this season, manager Craig Albernaz told Jake Rill of MLB.com. Holliday is getting more looks and options from doctors about what is going on with his injured left wrist, and the team is expecting to have more information later this week. The 22-year-old former first overall pick in 2022 got his 2026 season off on the wrong foot when he suffered a broken hamate bone in his hand, and he really has not been the same since this year. In his third year in the big leagues, Holliday will end up playing in only 98 games (354 plate appearances) while batting a disappointing .229/.300/.340 with a .640 OPS, seven home runs, 30 RBI, 45 runs scored, and eight stolen bases. There could still be a post-hype breakout coming for Holliday, but he will most likely be avoided in standard-sized fantasy baseball leagues next season until he can get back on track offensively.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Jake Rill
Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Out of Toronto's Lineup on Monday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 4:14 PM ET
Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (back) is missing from the team's starting nine for Monday's series opener on the road against the division-rival Baltimore Orioles, per MLB.com. Sean Keys will make the start at first base for Toronto and will bat fifth against Orioles right-hander Shane Baz at Camden Yards. Guerrero is dealing with more lower-back tightness and will sit out to begin the week after he was pulled from Sunday's game early against the Texas Rangers. Vladdy is considered day-to-day for now, but with Toronto's postseason hopes hanging by a thread going into the final week of the regular season, he could be shut down any day now if the Blue Jays are eliminated. Although Guerrero has looked much better in 18 games in September, the 2026 campaign has been a bitter disappointment for the 27-year-old Canadian, as he is currently slashing .263/.336/.359 with a .695 OPS, only nine home runs, 56 RBI, 71 runs scored, and seven stolen bases across his 529 at-bats. He has not hit more than two home runs in any month this season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Justin Verlander Scheduled to Make One More Start on Saturday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 3:30 PM ET
Detroit Tigers veteran right-hander Justin Verlander (hamstring, hip) is scheduled to come off the 60-day injured list to make one final start for his illustrious career on Saturday against the Pittsburgh Pirates, according to Jeff Seidel of The Detroit Free Press. Fantasy managers still competing for a championship in the final week of the regular season will obviously want to stay away, but it is something to watch for baseball fans this weekend in what will be the 43-year-old's final start in the big leagues before he hangs up his cleats. The former MVP, three-time Cy Young winner, and 10-time All-Star has made just one start this year, back on March 30 against the Arizona Diamondbacks, when he allowed five earned runs on six hits (one homer) while walking two and striking out one in just 3 2/3 innings of work. Verlander has been working his way back from hamstring and hip injuries all season, so we should not be expecting much out of him versus the Pirates.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Detroit Free Press - Jeff Seidel
MacKenzie Gore Scheduled to Start on Tuesday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 3:20 PM ET
The Texas Rangers announced on Monday that left-hander MacKenzie Gore (shoulder, back) is scheduled to make his next start on Tuesday against the New York Mets. Gore has checked out fine over the last few days and will be good to take the hill this week against the Mets after he dealt with some spasms in his upper back/shoulder area in his last start last Wednesday against the Boston Red Sox, when he went just four innings and threw 69 pitches. The matchup against New York is a good one as the Rangers seek to hold off the Houston Astros for the American League West title in the final week of the regular season, but Gore also carries significant risk coming off his injury last week. If the Rangers are still battling for a playoff spot this weekend, Gore could pitch in the final game of the regular season on Sunday against the Minnesota Twins, too. The 27-year-old southpaw has gone 8-11 this year with a career-high 4.67 ERA (3.89 FIP) and 1.35 WHIP with 172 strikeouts and 69 walks in 165 2/3 innings across 32 starts. Gore has allowed at least three earned runs with nine walks and only three strikeouts in his last three starts against the Red Sox, Arizona Diamondbacks, and Tampa Bay Rays.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Texas Rangers PR
Jesus Luzardo Cleared to Throw on Sunday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 11:33 AM ET
Philadelphia Phillies left-hander Jesus Luzardo (shoulder) was cleared to begin a throwing program on Sunday, according to Matt Gelb of The Athletic. Luzardo played catch with bullpen catcher Hector Rabago for around 10 minutes, which was the first time he had a full catch session in nine days. "Ready to go," president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski said. Luzardo has not pitched in a game since Sept. 7 due to inflammation in his left shoulder, and with the regular season coming to an end this weekend, he might not have enough time to get fully ramped up to rejoin the Phillies in a starting role if they make the postseason. Luzardo's next big test will be when he throws a bullpen session off a mound. He is eligible to come off the 15-day injured list for the final regular-season game, but the Phillies do not expect him to pitch in that game. Gelb writes that "all signs point" to the Phillies treating Luzardo as a reliever to begin the postseason. Getting Luzardo back at all next month would be a big boost to the Phillies' pitching staff, as the 28-year-old was one of the best pitchers in baseball in 2026, going 14-5 with a 2.87 ERA, 1.08 WHIP, and 221 strikeouts in 178 2/3 innings across his 29 starts.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Matt Gelb
Garrett Crochet Throws Two-Inning Side Session on Saturday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 11:27 AM ET
Boston Red Sox left-hander Garrett Crochet (shoulder) threw a two-inning side session on Saturday that consisted of around 20 pitches, according to Ian Browne of MLB.com. Crochet topped out at 92 mph. If he does not have any ill effects from that session, Boston is hopeful that Crochet can face hitters at Fenway Park this week, perhaps multiple times during the team's final homestand in the lead-up to the postseason in early October. The 27-year-old southpaw was the runner-up for the American League Cy Young Award in 2025 in his first season with the BoSox, but he has managed to make only six starts (30 innings) in his second year with the team due to shoulder and lat issues that have sidelined him since May. Crochet was not on his game before he landed on the injured list either, allowing 23 runs (21 earned) while walking 11 and striking out 37. Because he does not have enough time to get all the way stretched out in a starting role, the Red Sox are expecting to use Crochet out of the bullpen in the playoffs if he is cleared to pitch.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Ian Browne
Trent Grisham Not Expected to Return This Week


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 11:22 AM ET
New York Yankees outfielder Trent Grisham (hamstring) is not expected to be activated from the 10-day injured list before the end of the regular season this weekend, manager Aaron Boone told Bryan Hoch of MLB.com. However, it is still possible that Grisham will be on the playoff roster. The 29-year-old left-handed slugger has been sidelined since early September with a strained hamstring, and he will take this week to continue rehabbing in hopes of being included on the playoff roster in October. The two-time Gold Glover did not live up to his breakout season in the Bronx in 2025, when he hit a career-high 34 home runs and drove in 74 runs, as he will finish his 2026 campaign with a .211/.308/.395 slash line, 18 home runs, 59 RBI, 67 runs scored, and nine stolen bases in 121 games across 484 plate appearances. Grisham will likely operate as New York's center fielder against right-handed pitchers in the postseason if he gains clearance from his hamstring injury.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Bryan Hoch
Shane McClanahan Won't Return During Regular Season


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 11:04 AM ET
Tampa Bay Rays left-hander Shane McClanahan (forearm) will not return to pitch this week for the final week of the 2026 regular season, according to Marc Topkin of the Tampa Bay Times. Manager Kevin Cash said that McClanahan had a "good" throwing session on Friday, but he has been out since Sept. 4 with tightness in his left forearm, and he has run out of time to return to the major-league roster before the end of September. All in all, the 29-year-old two-time All-Star had a positive season in his return from Tommy John surgery that kept him out for each of the last two seasons. McClanahan ended up making 24 starts (118 innings) for the Rays this year and went 10-7 with a 3.36 ERA (3.50 FIP) and 1.12 WHIP with 106 strikeouts and 39 walks. The Rays are still hoping that McClanahan can return for their postseason run next month, but because he does not have time to get all the way built back up as a starter, he is expected to pitch out of the bullpen for Tampa in October.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Tampa Bay Times - Marc Topkin
Troy Melton Deals With Arm Discomfort in Final Start of Season


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 10:57 AM ET
Detroit Tigers right-hander Troy Melton (forearm) told reporters that he felt tightness in his forearm during his final start of the 2026 season on Sunday in an 8-1 loss to the division-rival Chicago White Sox, according to Chris McCosky of The Detroit News. The 25-year-old only went 3 2/3 innings, allowing four earned runs on four hits while walking three and striking out four for his fifth loss of the season. It is a disappointing way for Melton to end his year, but the good news is that he said he did not think his forearm tightness was related to the elbow issues he dealt with in the spring. "Yeah, I don't think it's going to be a long-term issue," Melton said. "The stuff is still good. I'm still throwing hard. Just the execution in the last few haven't been great." In his first 16 starts over 97 innings this year, Melton had a stingy 1.86 ERA while holding hitters to a .201 average and .607 OPS. But he struggled to close it out over his final three starts before Sunday's abbreviated outing, allowing 13 runs (11 earned), 18 hits, six walks, and three hit batsmen in 13 2/3 innings. When fully healthy, Melton is an intriguing arm for fantasy managers with a legitimate six-pitch mix and precise command of his four-seam fastball, sinker, and cutter.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Detroit News - Chris McCosky
River Ryan to Start for Tigers on Monday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 10:48 AM ET
Detroit Tigers right-handed pitching prospect River Ryan, who was acquired from the Los Angeles Dodgers in the blockbuster trade involving Tarik Skubal this summer, will make his Tigers debut on Monday and start against the Washington Nationals, according to Jason Beck of MLB.com. Right-hander Keider Montero will piggyback Ryan. Per MLB Pipeline, the 28-year-old former 11th-round pick by the San Diego Padres in 2021 is considered the Tigers' No. 3 prospect. He made his major-league debut with the Dodgers in 2024 and looked good in four starts, allowing four runs (three earned), walking nine, and striking out 18 in 20 1/3 innings pitched. Ryan has gone 3-1 on the farm in 2026 with a 4.39 ERA, 1.34 WHIP, and 47:9 K:BB in 41 innings across 10 starts with Triple-A Oklahoma City and Triple-A Toledo. He missed almost three months earlier this season with a hamstring injury, but he will try to finish off the year on a positive note back in the big leagues. Because Ryan will likely be limited to two or three innings on Monday, he will not be a realistic fantasy streamer in fantasy championship matchups.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Jason Beck

item.content:encoded:
Every Monday, this column will break down the most popular waiver wire and free agent acquisitions from the weekend. I dig into the top adds on the ever-popular Fantrax and in the NFBC Online Championship (OC), a national mid-stakes contest with 240 total leagues of 12 and a six-figure grand prize. Reviewing player adds between the two should provide us with a well-rounded perspective and barometer of the fantasy baseball marketplace.
Week 26 Overview
Hitters
The San Diego Padres took advantage of their four-game series with the Rockies at Coors Field and a home set with the Marlins, scoring 51 runs, 12 more than any other team. Fernando Tatis Jr. (along with Brandon Lowe and Pete Crow-Armstrong) led the way with a week-high four dingers. Last week’s streamers turned out to be dynamite: Jake Cronenworth (.464-8-2-8-2), Dustin Harris (.379-5-0-7-2) and Samad Taylor (.556-6-1-7-1) really stepped up, particularly Taylor for my competitive Main Event squad that gained two category points in batting average last week. Rake Cronenworth was true to his nickname from several years ago. He led all Major League hitters with 13 hits. The Brewers swiped a league-high 12 bags last week: four each for Jackson Chourio and rookie Cooper Pratt. Tampa’s Chandler Simpson led all runners with five swipes, finally catching Washington’s Nasim Nuñez for the MLB lead with 46. Expect Simpson to finish with 50+ and win the stolen base crown.
Pitchers
Of the 29 two-start pitchers excluding Pirates opener Lake Bachar, three earned two wins: Tarik Skubal, Sean Burke and David Peterson. Houston’s Hunter Brown had an outstanding two-step (10 IP – 5 H – 1 ER – 5 K – 20 K) and those 20 punchouts led all pitchers for the week. Gavin Williams punched out 16 in 12 innings and is back atop the AL lead in strikeouts with 244. Dylan Cease (239) may not make his final start of the season and Cam Schlittler (234) is unlikely to catch Williams as both have one start remaining. It’s very possible that Williams catches and passes Jacob Misiorowski (247) for the Major League lead. The Miz pitched three innings in his weekend start and might be limited for his final one.
Tampa’s Bryan Baker was the first reliever to reach 40 saves this season. It’s possible that Cade Smith (39), Riley O’Brien (38) and Mason Miller (37) join Baker. The last time there were three closers with 40 or more saves was in 2019: Edwin Díaz (57), Wade Davis (43), and Craig Kimbrel (42). Shout out to folks who drafted O’Brien late, and/or picked up Baker, Louis Varland or Jacob Latz off waivers and didn’t have to worry about the saves category all season.
Week 27 Most Added Players: NFBC Main Event, NFBC OC, and Fantrax
It’s the last hurrah for managers with FAB dollars left, hoping to get the best bang for the buck and for variance to lean their way and tip them into league titles. As is usually the case in the final week, we hope to optimize our pitching rotations and hitters in hitter-friendly ballparks against bad pitching. It was odd seeing Shohei Ohtani available in several leagues, and perhaps fortuitous as he should be activated this week and start a few games. Ohtani was acquired in 26 OCs for an AWB of $17. In Main Events, there were 12 shares available and they went for a reasonable $12 a pop. I scooped up a rare Ohtani share in an OC for $2, winning a tiebreaker over the team in 1st place in that league. Andy Pages will be activated on Tuesday, which should push Tommy Edman back to second base. Pages had been out since August 21, but was producing at an exciting clip before the injury — .272 – 72 R – 21 HR – 80 RBI – 12 SB in 550 PA. Managers who acquired him are hoping that he dusts the cobwebs back off and gets right into the swing of things, with all the marbles on the line.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Andy Pages | LAD | OF | 60% | $5 |
| 2 | JR Ritchie | ATL | SP | 57% | $3 |

| 6 | Heliot Ramos | NYY | OF | 35% | $7 |

| 11 | Pavin Smith | ARI | 1B | 30% | $4 |

AWB = Average Winning Bid (min: $4 AWB)
Pitchers were the most popular targets, specifically two-steppers, as we chase wins and strikeouts, hoping the Ratio Monster doesn’t eat our leads in ERA and WHIP. JR Ritchie and Daniel Lynch IV were the most added starters who we expect two starts from this week. Ritchie’s MLB debut back in April came with great promise, but walks haunted him greatly, which led to trips back to Triple-A to refine his craft and some bulk inning relief work when he returned to Atlanta in July. Ritchie was recently promoted again, and ran into a juggernaut Cubs offense last week, allowing six runs on seven hits in 4.2 innings. The walk rate (13.7%) isn’t pretty, and he has a good opportunity to end his season on a high note with two reasonable matchups — against the Reds at home and the Marlins on the road. Lynch had served the Royals well as their top southpaw out of the bullpen for most of the season. He moved to the rotation in August and slowly worked his pitch counts upward. Lynch has made it to five innings in each of his last three starts. His latest one (at HOU on September 16) went well — 5 IP – 2 H – 0 ER – 1 BB – 3 K. More of that please as he faces the White Sox and Guardians at Kauffman Stadium in the final week. If I could only choose one for the week, it would be Ritchie.
Red Sox pitchers Brayan Bello and Garrett Whitlock were popular buys as the likelihood of roto stars shining bright on them this week is high. Bello is coming off a tremendous outing against the AL-leading Rays on Saturday where he posted an 11:0 K:BB with just one run allowed in eight innings. Those 11 punchies tied his career high. Bello had been the worst starter in the game (6.49 ERA, 1.67 WHIP) through June 4, when he was optioned to Triple-A. Since the All-Star break, mostly out of relief and with two starts, the 27-year-old has been shining. Over those 51.1 innings, he is rocking exemplary ratios (2.28 ERA, 1.01 WHIP) and a 17% K-BB% (22.3% K, 5.3% BB). Bello should make a start against the Cubs next Saturday. The Cubs should be settled into a playoff spot by then, so perhaps they give Pete Crow-Armstrong and some of the other regulars that day off. Boston’s closer Aroldis Chapman has been day-to-day with a lat issue, so perhaps the Red sox have him take it easy and provide Whitlock with some save opportunities. Whitlock has a 7-2 record with a 17.5 ERA, 0.88 WHIP and four saves.
Streaming Diamondbacks is a good idea this week, specifically for their three-game set at Coors Field against the Rockies in the early part of the week. Pavin Smith was a coveted target, coming off a four-day stretch where three of his hits were home runs. Don’t expect Smith to start against lefty Kyle Freeland, but he should be in the lineup for the other two contests against righties. Nolan Arenado was available in one of the 60 Main Event leagues and was acquired for just one dollar.
Better late than never for two punchless Padres who have been quite productive and certainly enjoyed their visit to Coors Field in the first half of last week. Dustin Harris ($10 AWB) and Samad Taylor ($5) have been red hot and playing often over the last 10 days. Though he doesn’t have a home run yet, Harris has been quite productive and helpful to early-bird managers: eight runs, 12 runs batted in and three steals, batting .384 with a 166 wRC+ in 40 plate appearances since September 11. He’s also been batting second against right-handed starters. Taylor has at least one hit in nine of his last 10, including a 3-for-3 effort on Sunday, and has driven in seven in his last seven games.

item.content:encoded:
What to watch for as the playoffs loom: Phillies counting on Alex McFarlane, starters as relievers, and more
With their magic number down to three, a fifth straight postseason is in sight for the Phillies. But there are plenty of questions going into the final homestand of the regular season.
The Phillies returned from their final road trip of the season with work to do.
Their magic number to clinch a postseason berth is three. Any combination of wins and Diamondbacks losses that totals three will ensure the Phillies’ season continues beyond Sunday. But while they remain in control of their own destiny, it won’t be easy.
To close out the final week, the Phillies host the top team in the National League in the Brewers, followed by the top team in the American League in the Rays.
Here are a few takeaways heading into the last homestand of the regular season:
Multi-inning McFarlane
The circle of trust in the Phillies bullpen right now is extremely small. The relief unit has a 5.50 ERA in September, and the club took the drastic measure of optioning Orion Kerkering to triple-A Lehigh Valley on Sunday after his struggles became untenable. Unless there is an injury to another member of the staff, he is ineligible to be on the wild-card roster.
While the Phillies’ rotation and closer Jhoan Duran are among the best in the sport, it’s the bridge between them that has been the biggest issue. The Phillies continue to hope Jonathan Bowlan (groin) will be available for the postseason. The right-hander began playing catch Sunday, and reported to the field on Monday’s off day to continue his progress.
Before the injury, Bowlan had been going through a rough stretch, having allowed a run in five of his last six appearances. Even if he were a full go, it would be hard to imagine tossing him right back into an eighth-inning, high-leverage role after spending some time on the shelf.
» READ MORE: Phillies send struggling reliever Orion Kerkering to triple A
Enter Alex McFarlane.
The 25-year-old rookie came through in a big spot against the Mets on Sunday, facing two tough opponents in Francisco Lindor and Juan Soto to get out of a seventh-inning jam. By retiring both of them, McFarlane added a few more notches to his belt, which already included such stars as Shohei Ohtani, Mike Trout, and Nolan Arenado.
But Sunday’s win over the Mets also revealed how interim manager Don Mattingly is planning to handle his relievers in the postseason. After McFarlane struck out Soto to preserve a two-run lead with his 18th pitch, there was initially no movement in the Phillies’ bullpen during the eighth. When the Phillies loaded the bases, that’s when Chase Shugart started getting ready.
Had the Phillies’ lead stayed at two, though, Mattingly was going to send McFarlane back out. Duran would have then started warming to relieve him, and then finish it off in the ninth.
It didn’t wind up happening, but Mattingly envisions using McFarlane and Duran to cover the last nine outs of a close game.
“I think it is [realistic] this time of year,” Mattingly said. “I mean, I think with Jho, you also get to the point where he’s capable of two innings. You’re just trying to get the guys that we need in the game, for as much as you can.”
So while the lack of relief depth is still a concern, things will operate a bit differently in the playoffs. The trusted high-leverage arms, as few as they are, can and will be called upon to do more.
» READ MORE: Don Mattingly thinks Chase Shugart can take on a bigger role in Phillies' bullpen
McFarlane has thrown more than one inning just once in the two months he’s been in the majors, covering 1⅓ innings Aug. 15 against the Twins. He said he is ready to do whatever he’s asked.
“Just grateful for the opportunity,” McFarlane said. “Whatever opportunity he gives me, I’m just gonna take it one game at a time. Make sure I prepare my best, and just give all I can anytime he sends me out there.”
Starters in relief
The Phillies still haven’t mapped out how they will deploy their rotation in a wild-card series. That’s because there are a lot of unknowns: whether they will make it at all, who they will play if they do, and the health of Jesús Luzardo.
The club is “very optimistic” about Luzardo’s progress from the shoulder inflammation that landed him on the injured list, according to president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski. Like Bowlan, he has also progressed to playing catch.
Should Luzardo remain on track to return in time for the postseason, Dombrowski said the Phillies are keeping their options open with how they deploy him. It could be as a starter, which might be a risk given his last outing will have been Sept. 7. It could also be as a reliever, a role Luzardo has less experience in, but experience nonetheless. In the deciding Game 4 of the 2025 National League Division Series, he held off the Dodgers for 1⅔ innings of emergency relief in extras, pitching on short rest.
» READ MORE: The Zack Wheeler conversation: Why he ‘expected’ to thrive after surgery, and how much longer he wants to play
His performance in that role was largely overshadowed by how the game ended, with Kerkering botching a bases-loaded grounder to allow Los Angeles to walk it off. Had Kerkering made the throw to end the inning and things turned out differently, Luzardo’s clutch bullpen appearance might have gone down as legendary instead.
Whether or not Luzardo is one of them, the Phillies bullpen will be getting reinforcements by way of the rotation for the postseason. The question is who.
“Some of our starters are going to end up in the bullpen,” Dombrowski said. “I don’t know how it’s going to work at this point, but some of them will, especially when you get to the first round. We’re going to be the best-of-three, so you only can start three guys at that point. So you got two other guys that can go into the bullpen.”
It’s difficult to see a world where Zack Wheeler or Cristopher Sánchez aren’t starting two of the wild-card games. Aaron Nola has continued his second-half resurgence with a 2.15 ERA since Aug. 3, but he has never been a reliever in any capacity during his major league career, regular season or postseason.
Rookie Andrew Painter continues to be under consideration for making the move. He gave up four runs in his last start against the Mets, but the quality of his stuff remained high. Painter’s first inning especially stood out, when he got Lindor to ground out before striking out Soto and Bo Bichette.
Painter touched 99.4 mph with his fastball in the fifth inning. In a shorter stint, it isn’t hard to imagine him getting into the triple digits.
“I think his stuff will be very solid out there,” Dombrowski said.
» READ MORE: Andrew Painter’s potential role on a Phillies playoff staff is uncertain. Painter says any role is OK with him.
If the opportunity arises in the final six games, Mattingly said he could see the Phillies test-driving that theory by trying Painter out in the bullpen ahead of the playoffs. That said, time is running out.
Painter doesn’t think he necessarily needs a trial run to feel comfortable pitching in relief, however. He has experience with his routine shifting already, pitching behind an opener earlier this year and also appearing in relief after being scratched from his start because of a migraine.
“I feel like postseason baseball, in that atmosphere, the adrenaline is going to be flowing,” Painter said. “I don’t really think there’s much of an adjustment that’s going to be there. I think the adrenaline would just take over from that point.”
More patience from Turner
Whether the Phillies’ offense will get hot at the right time or slide back into a familiar October slumber remains to be seen. But there were some positive signs, particularly from the top of their order, in the series against the Mets.
En route to the series split, it was the top half of the order that carried a lot of the load — excluding a key bases-loaded triple from nine-hole hitter Justin Crawford on Sunday. And that’s how it will need to be for the Phillies to make a deep run.
They didn’t do it with the long ball, as the Phillies’ only two home runs in the series came from Derek Hill and Edmundo Sosa. Instead, they got on base, moved runners, and strung together hits.
Trea Turner in particular had a strong series. He finished 4-for-13 (.308), but the real eye-popping stat was his .526 on-base percentage.
» READ MORE: Can Trea Turner rescue his season despite career-worst stats at the plate? His manager and teammates believe so.
If he could maintain some of that momentum, it would be transformative for the Phillies. What has been a disappointing season by most measures for Turner could be rescued with a strong postseason performance.
“I think more and more, you see how they’re pitching him, and it’s I think basically not throwing him strikes,” Mattingly said of Turner.
According to StatCast, 53.6% of the pitches Turner has seen this year are out of the strike zone. It’s a few percentage points higher than the 51.3% out-of-zone pitches he saw last year, and trails only Kyle Schwarber (54.8%) and Bryce Harper (57.4%) among Turner’s teammates.
The difference has been that Turner swings at those out-of-zone pitches at a much higher clip. His chase rate this year is 34.6%, the second-highest of his career.
But against the Mets, he showed a glimpse of what he could be if he homes in on his selectivity. Turner drew six walks in the four-game series. He also scored three runs.
“The more he walks, the more they’re forced in the strike zone,” Mattingly said. “And when he’s on base, obviously it creates a danger there with him running and things like that. We need him to get on base. When he’s on base, we’re better.”

We’ve made it to the final week of the regular season. There are still two divisions in the American League up for grabs, a couple of long-shot playoff hopefuls looking to make a last-minute run, and playoff seeding to fight over. It should make for a dramatic end to a great season.
Our power rankings use a modified Elo rating system. If you’re familiar with chess rankings, you’ll know that Elo is an elegant ranking format that measures teams’ relative strength and is very reactive to recent performance. To avoid overweighting recent results during the season, we weigh each team’s raw Elo rank using our coin flip playoff odds (specifically, we regress the playoff odds by 50% and weigh those against the raw Elo ranking, increasing in weight as the season progresses to a maximum of 25%). The weighted Elo ranks are then displayed as “Power Score” in the tables below. As the best and worst teams sort themselves out between now and October, they’ll filter to the top and bottom of the rankings, while the exercise remains reactive to hot streaks and cold snaps. If you’re looking for a visual representation of the ups and downs of your team throughout the season, look no further than the brand new Power Rankings Board in the FanGraphs Lab.
First up are the full rankings, presented in a sortable table. Below that, I’ve grouped the teams into tiers with comments on a handful of clubs. You’ll notice that the official ordinal rankings don’t always match the tiers — there are times where I take editorial liberties when grouping teams together — but generally, the ordering is consistent. One thing to note: The playoff odds listed in the tables below are our standard Depth Charts odds, not the coin flip odds that are used in the ranking formula.

It was a great week for the Brewers. They won their fourth straight NL Central title and sixth in the last nine years, and also set another franchise record for wins in a single season, one year after setting the previous record. They now have a chance to win 100 games for the first time in club history this week and still have the top seed in the NL to play for.
The Rays swept the Athletics and won their series against the Red Sox last week to put some distance between themselves and the Yankees in the AL East race. The gap in the division is now six games, and even though the two rivals play each other four times during the final week of the season, it would take a massive collapse from Tampa Bay to upset the current standings. Because the Rays also currently lead the season series with the Yankees, 6-3, all they need is to win one of the four games in New York to take the division title. With Shane McClanahan still recovering from his forearm injury — his availability for the playoffs is up in the air — Freddy Peralta has stepped up to lead the pitching staff over the last few weeks. Across his last five starts, he’s allowed just three runs in 28 2/3 innings. That’s the kind of production the Rays were hoping to get when they acquired him at the trade deadline.

The Dodgers are getting all their pieces in place for the postseason. Andy Pages and Roki Sasaki will be activated off the IL on Tuesday, and Shohei Ohtani should follow on Wednesday. There’s a lingering question about Blake Snell’s status after he injured his groin last week, but it sounds like he’ll be able to make a start during the final weekend of the season. And even though the majority of the year has been a slog for Kyle Tucker, his bat seems to have finally woken up at the right time; he collected nine hits and three home runs last week.
Having won 13 of their last 14 games, the Padres are peaking at exactly the right moment. They’ve surged five games ahead of the Diamondbacks and one ahead of the Phillies in the NL Wild Card standings, and are now tied with the Cubs for the top spot. San Diego’s final series of the season against Arizona still looms large, especially if the Friars stumble against the Dodgers in the series beforehand. You’re probably familiar with Fernando Tatis Jr.’s hot streak — he blasted four home runs last week to bring his total in September up to eight — but the biggest contributor to the Padres’ success recently has been Ty France. He had 12 hits and a home run last week and has posted a fantastic 168 wRC+ during the second half of the season.
After a couple of years away from the top, the Braves are NL East champions again — it’s their seventh division title in the last nine years. Atlanta’s dominance this year has been a welcome return to form. Even though his season has been a bit up and down, Ronald Acuña Jr. is looking like the superstar that won the MVP back in 2023 again. Last week, he smacked three home runs, including a go-ahead grand slam on Saturday, and is running a 191 wRC+ in September.
A little more than a week after being activated off the IL, Aaron Judge is back on the shelf, this time with a calf injury sustained on Wednesday. His availability for the playoffs is still up in the air, though he’s confident that he’ll be able to return sooner rather than later. Thankfully, Jazz Chisholm Jr. should be activated off the IL on Tuesday, and there’s some confidence that Trent Grisham will also be ready to return for the postseason. It helps that Ben Rice has bounced back from a rough August to post a 192 wRC+ in September. Still, Judge’s injury is a major blow to the Yankees’ hopes for a deep October run.

Even though the Red Sox lost both of their series last week, they managed to clinch a postseason berth on Sunday. It’s the cap to a remarkable turnaround after the team looked completely lost in mid-June. Boston can officially secure the second Wild Card spot with a couple of wins against the Guardians this week. Then the team can turn its attention to the Yankees and the rematch of last year’s Wild Card matchup between these two historic rivals.
Nothing is going to come easy for the Phillies over the next few weeks. The team placed Jesús Luzardo on the IL last week with a shoulder injury, but thankfully, it sounds like he’ll be ready to pitch in the playoffs. But before they count their chickens, they need to actually clinch a playoff spot. Philadelphia is four games up on the Diamondbacks in the NL Wild Card race, but its upcoming opponents are no cake walk; the Phillies have the Brewers and Rays on the schedule to finish off the regular season. Facing two of the best teams in baseball is quite a test ahead of the postseason, and the Phillies haven’t exactly been playing well lately.
The biggest concern for the Cubs right now is the status of Alex Bregman. He was struck by a foul ball in the face while standing in the on-deck circle during Sunday’s game and was taken to the hospital for further evaluation. Alongside Pete Crow-Armstrong, Bregman has been one of the best hitters in baseball since the All-Star break. It would be a huge blow if the third baseman had to miss any significant amount of time at this point in the season. As for Crow-Armstrong, he’s two stolen bases away from joining the 40/40 club. La jugada que terminó por cambiar el rumbo del encuentro llegó en la quinta entrada. Los Diamondbacks habían conseguido llenar las bases frente al abridor de Nueva York, Will Warren, quien dejó el montículo para darle paso al relevista Brent Headrick.
El pitcher logró retirar a Geraldo Perdomo con un ponche para conseguir el segundo out, pero después vino el descontrol. Headrick otorgó una base por bolas a Corbin Carroll, situación que permitió que Arizona sumara una carrera y dejara las bases listas para Arenado.
Con cuenta de 2-1, el tercera base no perdonó. Arenado encontró el lanzamiento y mandó la pelota por encima de la barda para completar el grand slam y darle la vuelta al partido. Fue el noveno cuadrangular con las bases llenas de su carrera, además de que alcanzó al cubano Yordan Álvarez, de los Houston Astros, como líder de las Grandes Ligas en grand slams durante esta temporada.
Pero el poder ofensivo de Arizona no se limitó a Arenado. Perdomo también tuvo una tarde productiva al conectar un sencillo productor en la primera entrada y posteriormente un triple que llevó otra carrera al plato durante el séptimo episodio.
Los Yankees, por su parte, habían respondido con fuerza en el tercer inning. Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. y Spencer Jones conectaron cuadrangulares consecutivos dentro de esa entrada frente al abridor de Arizona, Corbin Burnes, para mantener con vida a Nueva York.
Sin embargo, la ofensiva neoyorquina se apagó después de ese episodio. El bullpen de Arizona tomó el control y, encabezado por Justin Martínez, consiguió limitar a los Yankees a solamente tres imparables durante las últimas 6 entradas. Martínez se apuntó la victoria, la tercera de su temporada, con marca de 3-0.

PHOENIX — The Yankees' chances of winning the AL East title were reduced to nearly zero on Sunday . . . not that they were all that good to begin with.
The Tampa Bay Rays entered Sunday with a magic number of four to eliminate the Yankees from contention for first place. That became three when the Rays beat the Red Sox, and it dropped to two when the Yankees lost to the Arizona Diamondbacks, 8-4.
The Rays (95-60) lead the Yankees (89-66) by six games with seven to play. The two teams will play four games in the Bronx this week, including a split doubleheader on Tuesday. If the Rays win that first game — or any game in the series — the race is over. The Yankees must win all four games to stay alive, and a sweep also would give them the tiebreaker in the season series, 7-6.
The Yankees are scheduled to start lefthanders Carlos Rodon (6-3, 2.95 ERA) and Max Fried (5-4, 2.63) on Tuesday against the Rays, who will counter with righthanders Nick Martinez (15-4, 2.94) and Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72). Gerrit Cole and Cam Schlittler are slated to pitch Wednesday and Thursday for the Yankees.
The Yankees did reduce their magic number to clinch the first wild card — and home-field advantage in the Wild Card Round — to one over the Red Sox, whom they seem likely to play in that round for the second straight season.
The Yankees managed only three hits in the final 6 1/3 innings after hitting three no-doubt home runs off Corbin Burnes in the third inning — 388 feet to left by Heliot Ramos (107.6-mph exit velocity), 424 to left by George Lombard Jr. (108.7) and 448 to center by Spencer Jones (109.8) — for a 4-1 lead, but Arizona's Nolan Arenado capped a five-run fifth with a two-out grand slam off Brent Headrick.
Yankees starter Will Warren retired Tim Tawa to begin the fifth, but Lars Nootbaar doubled, Ketel Marte singled and Gabriel Moreno walked to load the bases. Headrick replaced Warren and struck out Geraldo Perdomo for the second out, but he walked Corbin Carroll to force in a run. One pitch after Arenado's bid for a grand slam went just foul, he gave the Diamondbacks a 6-4 lead with a blast to leftfield.
Perdomo had a run-scoring single in the first and an RBI triple in the seventh as Arizona recorded its MLB-best 47th comeback victory of the season.

PHOENIX -- The sound off the bat got an eruption of sound from the Chase Field crowd. But as the ball off the bat of Nolan Arenado traveled toward the left-foul pole, it began to hook. It ultimately slid foul, almost a go-ahead grand slam in the bottom of the fifth that would have kept the D-backs’ postseason chances alive.
One pitch later, Arenado hammered the next one fair into the left-field seats. Pendulum, swung.
It marked Arenado’s ninth career grand slam and third this year, tying Paul Goldschmidt (2013) and Eugenio Suárez (2025) for the most in a single season in franchise history. It was the turning point in the club’s 8-4 victory over the Yankees on Sunday during the 2026 regular-season home finale, marking their 47th comeback win of the year, the most in the Majors.
But with the Cubs (87-69), Padres (87-69) and Phillies (86-70) all winning on Sunday as well, the D-backs remain four games out of the third and final National League Wild Card spot with just six games to play. To paraphrase Yankees Hall of Famer Yogi Berra and one of his “Yogi-isms”:
“It’s getting late early.”
While the D-backs will conclude the regular season with a three-game series against San Diego next week, they trail the Padres by five games. That means Arizona will need to make up two games in the standings by the time it arrives at Petco Park next Friday to give themselves a chance at October baseball.
Regardless of what the next week holds for the 2026 D-backs as they embark on the road, what can’t be denied is that by virtue of their 45-37 record at Chase Field, they turned in the most successful season at home since 2017 (53-29).

The final road game of the 2026 regular season is upon us, as the Yankees will conclude it with a seven-game homestand before likely hosting the Red Sox for the Wild Card Series. If the season ends there, this is the end of the line for the gray uniforms for 2026, but obviously, we all hope we’ll see them next in Tampa (and more) in early October.
Looking to end a road slate that has been very generous to the Yankees on a high note is Will Warren, who’s finishing his sophomore season strong after his great start to the campaign unraveled into a bit of a mess over the summer. Rotation reinforcements that threatened to throw him in the bullpen never came with the recurring injuries, so he’ll finish 2026 with 30 starts for the second straight season. This is No. 29, as he enters with a 3.89 ERA (108 ERA+) and 4.07 FIP in 148 innings. No matter what happens from here, Warren has had a successful year in solidifying himself as a true MLB-caliber rotation arm.
Opposing him will be a former Cy Young winner trying to round into form off Tommy John surgery in Corbin Burnes, whom Yankees fans remember well from his lone season in Baltimore in 2024. Returning from a 16-month absence on September 8 to help with the playoff push, Burnes has allowed five runs across 7.2 innings with six strikeouts to two walks against the Royals and Marlins. He isn’t totally built up, having thrown 75 pitches in his last start, so expect him to settle around 80-85 today. He’s always befuddled the Yankees, pitching to a 1.93 ERA across 23.1 innings in his career, but he doesn’t have a win in any of those four starts.
Ben Rice will once again lead off, followed by Cody Bellinger, Heliot Ramos, and Luis García Jr. We’ve seen better ABs and swings from George Lombard Jr. lately, who’ll bat fifth. Spencer Jones is back after a one-day absence due to a sore foot and will bat in front of Anthony Volpe, Austin Wells, and José Caballero.
Lars Nootbaar will also be a repeat leadoff hitter for the D-backs, followed by Ketel Marte, Gabriel Moreno, and Geraldo Perdomo. Corbin Carroll is batting fifth, Nolan Arenado will bat sixth, and former Blue Jay Jesús Sánchez bats seventh ahead of last night’s hero Pavin Smith and Tim Tawa.

The Arizona Diamondbacks are fighting for their playoff lives and were counting on Corbin Burnes to come back and help them in September.
Unfortunately he's been anything but a help to the team's push to make the Postseason.
Corbin Burnes Gets Hammered by Yankees
Burnes wiggled out of a first-inning jam when he allowed a walk and a single to start the game. But he retired the next three batters and pitched a scoreless second inning as well.
Burnes appeared to be cruising when he got two quick outs in the third too, but then disaster struck. Heliot Ramos launched a line drive homer 107 MPH off the bat into the left field bleachers to tie the game at 1-1. It came on a middle-middle 92 MPH sinker.
A sharp base hit by Luis Garcia Jr. followed, and Torey Lovullo got the pen up, as Ryne Nelson began throwing. But George Lombard hit a 91 MPH cutter, also in the middle of the plate, 20 rows up, 424 feet out to left for a two-run blast.
That would not be the end of Burnes' torture. The very next batter, Spencer Jones, went down and got a curveball at the bottom of the zone, crushing it 448 feet onto the concourse in left center field.
That was all for Burnes, who was pulled from the game with a pitching line of 2.2 innings, five runs on four hits, including the three homers. He left the game trailing 4-1, handing it off to Nelson. Nolan Arenado hit a grand slam in the fifth inning to put the D-backs ahead 6-4 and get Burnes off the won-loss hook.
Rough Road to Recovery
It's been a rough road to recovery for Burnes, who suffered an elbow injury on June 1 of last year. He was attempting to return from Tommy John surgery by the All-Star break this year, but a shoulder injury dealt him a setback.
Somewhat controversially, the D-backs ended up rushing Burnes through his rehab process, bringing him back before he was fully stretched out.
He was finally able to make his season debut on September 8, throwing three scoreless innings. His next outing went poorly however, as he went 4.2 innings and allowed five runs on five hits and two homers.
Burnes has now allowed nine runs in 10.1 innings, for a 7.84 ERA, giving up five homers in the process. His velocity on the cutter, already down to a career low 92.7 coming into Sunday's game, bottomed out at 90.9.
The movement profile on his signature pitch is a shadow of it's former self as well. Simply put, the cutter doesn't cut right now. A right-handers cutter, by definition should break glove side.
Fully 34% of his cutters thrown heading into today were actually moving to the arm side, not glove side. In Sunday's outing, 19 of 39, 48% of cutters broke armside. During his peak years that number was about 2-3%, but had crept up to 11-16% in recent years prior to 2026.
D-backs fans were warned by this publication not to set expectations too high for a starter returning mid-season from Tommy John surgery. That's certainly been the case this year.
Perhaps after a full off-season throwing program and spring training, Burnes can regain his form. That's if there is no lockout interrupting Spring Training, of course.
Burnes won the NL Cy Young in 2021 and was one of the most durable pitchers in the game prior to signing with the Diamondbacks during the 2024-25 offseason. He is still owed four years, $140 million on his contract after this season. He has an opt-out that he will certainly not be exercising. The D-backs can only hope that he'll be able to help next year.

The Arizona Diamondbacks are 4.0 games back in the NL Wild Card race as the final week's worth of games are set to get underway.
As Arizona's working their way back into contention, one of the most important contributors has been Nolan Arenado. But they almost didn't have him for this stretch of the year.
According to USA Today's Bob Nightengale, Arenado could've landed on the injured list a few weeks ago, but refused the Diamondbacks' wish to place him on the IL. That refusal has borne fruit, as the future Hall of Famer has been incredible for the D-Backs lately.
Diamondbacks are fortunate Nolan Arenado refused placement on IL
"The Diamondbacks wanted to place Arenado on the IL a few weeks ago with a left intercostal injury and an inflamed thumb, but he refused, insisting he could play through the injuries in the pennant race," Nightengale writes.
Arenado has been a solid contributor for the Diamondbacks overall this season, and it would make sense for Arizona to protect the veteran third baseman if he wasn't 100%.
But Arenado didn't want to hit the injured list, refusing a potential placement on the IL. That refusal has been a major boost for Arizona.
Since the start of September, roughly around when the Diamondbacks would've asked Arenado to hit the IL, he's been one of the best hitters in MLB.
In 16 games and 56 at-bats, Arenado has 18 hits, seven runs scored, two doubles, five home runs, nine RBIs, seven walks, a .321 batting average, and a 1.031 OPS.
If it wasn't for Arenado playing at such a high level, the Diamondbacks might've been much farther back than four games, as they enter play on Sunday, September 20.
While the Diamondbacks' postseason future is still up in the air, Arenado's decision to refuse to hit the injured list has proven to be the right call so far.

By DAVID BRANDT
PHOENIX (AP) — Pavin Smith hit a two-run homer in the ninth inning to lift the Arizona Diamondbacks over the New York Yankees 5-3 on Saturday night, giving the D-backs’ slim playoff hopes a boost.
Ildemaro Vargas started the ninth with a walk, winning an ABS challenge on a full-count pitch initially called a strike. After Jordan Lawlar struck out, Smith pinch hit and drove a cutter from Michael Fulmer (0-1) into the right-field seats.
Arizona pulled within four games of Philadelphia for the final NL wild card with seven games remaining, snapping a three-game losing streak on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of its 2001 World Series win over the Yankees.
Juan Morillo (1-1) pitched 1 1/3 hitless innings. D-backs right-hander Brandon Pfaadt gave up one run on four hits and a walk over 4 1/3 innings, striking out three.
New York’s 11 walk-off losses are one behind San Francisco, which has the most in the major leagues.
New York ace Cam Schlittler gave up three runs — but only one earned — over six innings. The right-hander allowed three hits and three walks, striking out six and lowering his ERA to 1.94.
Schlitter’s 24 starts with one or no earned runs this year is one shy of the record in the live-ball era since 1920, set by Sandy Koufax in 1963, according to Major League Baseball.
The All-Star didn’t allow a hit until the fifth inning when Nolan Arenado lined a one-out single into left field. The right-hander then made a costly error on Tim Tawa’s sacrifice bunt attempt, dropping the ball as he tried to throw to first. Jordan Lawlar capitalized on the miscue with a two-out triple into the left-center field gap for a 2-1 lead.
Austin Wells and Heliot Ramos hit solo homers off Kevin Ginkel in the sixth to push the Yankees ahead 3-2.
Corbin Carroll hit a sacrifice fly in the bottom half but Schlittler limited damage by striking out Arenado and Tawa to end the threat.

As Guardians chase playoff spot, Jose Ramirez records career RBI 1,000
CLEVELAND — Cleveland’s baseball franchise has never had a player quite like Jose Ramirez.
Along with signing under-market contracts to remain with the Guardians twice and the many memorable moments in a Cleveland uniform over the past decade-plus, his assault on the record books added another chapter Sept. 18 in a 5-3 win over the Athletics, which allowed them to retake the lead in the American League Central race with eight game remaining.
In that win, Ramirez went 2-for-5 with a home run and two RBIs, which gave him 1,000 RBIs in his career. In doing so, he became the 12th active player to reach 1,000 RBIs, joining Freddie Freeman, Paul Goldschmidt, Manny Machado, Giancarlo Stanton, Mike Trout, Bryce Harper, Nolan Arenado, Andrew McCutchen, Salvador Perez, Eugenio Suarez and Carlos Santana.
“Very important to thank God for that opportunity to play here in this organization and to be bale to achieve that,” Ramirez said through a team translator. “But the most important part is that we’re able to win today because you guys know what I really want to do here, which is win.”
Jose Ramirez stats
He’s also just the second Cleveland player to hit that milestone with the franchise, joining Earl Averill (1,084), whose playing career ended in the early 1940s.
It’s a significant line on Ramirez's Hall of Fame resume. The home run also brought him within three of becoming only the ninth player in MLB history to reach the 300/300 club for home runs and stolen bases.
“I like to use round numbers,” Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. “It’s 10 years of 100 RBIs. When you break it down that way, it’s incredible what he has accomplished, and he’s not even close to being done. And very few people get do it, and it’s really cool to be here to watch it.”
It was a milestone night for Ramirez, though it came at the end of what has been one of his more frustrating seasons, particularly over the last few weeks while he’s played through hamate been surgery rehab.
Jose Ramirez injury update
He’s posted a 90 wRC+, which would be the first time since he became a full-time player in 2016 he’s been below 100 (league average). Since he returned to the lineup on July 22, after the procedure, he’s hit .216 with a .567 OPS.
“I keep working on it every day,” Ramirez said. “I have to keep working in the training room every day because this type of injury is the type where one day you feel good, the next you don’t feel so well, but you have to keep grinding.”
Despite the lack of his usual MVP-caliber production on a nightly basis, Vogt and the Guardians have still applauded the way Ramirez has fought through the situation. It’s one of the attributes that often gets mentioned first when listing why they feel he’s so valuable to the organization.
“Even as he was coming back and we have to give him off days, he was not happy about it,” Vogt said. “He wants to play every day. He wants to give us everything that he has on any given day. We know that there’s days where he’s not feeling good and he still goes out and gives 100 percent of what he has that day.
“It’s such a great example for our young guys to see that just because you’re not feeling 100 percent, it doesn’t mean you can’t go out and compete and contribute to help the team win.”
Ryan Lewis covers the Guardians for the Beacon Journal. He can be reached at rlewis1@gannett.com.

CLEVELAND -- As the Progressive Field crowd roared around him, José Ramírez paused and leaned back in the left-handed batter’s box to admire his work. There was no doubt where the baseball he launched to right field was headed.
That image has played on repeat over the past 14 seasons. This time, it came with a heavy dose of history, and it was well-timed as the Guardians continue to push for the postseason.
Ramírez tallied his 1,000th career RBI on Friday by launching his 297th career home run, in the sixth inning of the Guardians’ matchup with the A’s in the opener of a three-game series. The superstar third baseman joined Earl Averill (1,084) as the only players in Cleveland franchise history to hit the RBI milestone.
The Guardians improved to 79-75 with their third straight win. They entered Friday with the same record as the White Sox, but Chicago technically led the division because it holds the tiebreaker over Cleveland after winning the season series.
It means the Guardians must finish with more wins than the Sox to win the Central for a third straight year. Ramírez helped; his towering blast went a Statcast-projected 401 feet and had a 102.4 mph exit velocity.
Ramírez, who turned 34 years old on Thursday, is now just the 12th active player with 1,000 career RBIs, joining Freddie Freeman, Paul Goldschmidt, Nolan Arenado, Manny Machado, Giancarlo Stanton, Andrew McCutchen, Carlos Santana, Bryce Harper, Salvador Perez, Mike Trout and Eugenio Suárez.
The home run was Ramírez’s first since Aug. 30 and just his 12th this season. He entered Friday with an uncharacteristic .683 OPS in 117 games, in an injury-impacted campaign after he missed five weeks following left hamate surgery.
Ramírez has been dealt with the effects of that procedure since he came off the injured list on July 22. On Friday, he reminded us he’s always just one swing away from impacting a game in a big way.

Top MLB home run picks for Friday, Sept. 18
- Nolan Arenado, Diamondbacks (+630, DraftKings)
- Mike Yastrzemski, Braves (+630, FanDuel)
Nolan Arenado, Diamondbacks (+630, DraftKings)
An important series in the desert opens tonight, and I'm sure there will be sellouts all weekend as the New York Yankees make a rare visit to Phoenix with a 9:40 ET first pitch. There are no weather concerns as Chase Field has a usually-closed retractable roof. It's not out of the question this could be a World Series preview. New York will be in the AL playoffs, most likely as the AL's top wild card team. Arizona has work to do to earn the NL's last wild card spot over San Diego.
And we get a Hall-of-Fame-caliber matchup in the bottom of the first in Yankees right-hander Gerrit Cole facing Diamondbacks third baseman Nolan Arenado. The one reason Cole might not get to Cooperstown is because his career is cut a bit short after injuries cost the 2023 Cy Young winner a chunk of the 2024 season and all of 2025. The 36-year-old righty has been moderately back in form this year at 8-9 with a 3.67 ERA. but has also allowed 20 homers in 20 starts.
Perhaps Cole is tiring as he has been ravaged for seven homers in back-to-back losses, allowing nine runs and 15 hits over 11 1/3 innings. In his most recent start against the Mets, Cole managed only three swings and misses, none generated by Cole's 38 fastballs.
There is no doubt Arenado will be headed to Cooperstown as arguably a top-10 third baseman in MLB history as a 10-time All-Star, eight-time Gold Glover, five-time Silver Slugger Award winner and three-time NL home run leader. The 35-year-old has one year left on that eight-year, $260 million contract originally signed with the Rockies in 2019. Arenado's 26 homers this season, his first with Arizona, are his most since 26 in 2023 with the Cardinals. He has hit 15 of those 26 at home and is 10-for-22 in his career off Cole with three homers and two doubles, good for a slugging percentage of .955.
Perhaps also consider a longshot flier on Snakes catcher James McCann, even though he only has five homers and doesn't play all the time. McCann is 6-for-14 with three doubles and a homer career off Cole.
Mike Yastrzemski, Braves (+630, FanDuel)
It's a matchup of division leaders tonight to open a series as Atlanta visits Houston with an 8:10 ET first pitch, and the Daikin Park retractable roof is usually closed. These clubs are division leaders in very different senses. The Braves will win the NL East, while the Astros are neck-and-neck with the Rangers in the AL West and could miss the postseason entirely.
The Braves already did the Astros a solid for this series by opting to skip ace Chris Sale in it. That somewhat hints to me what Atlanta's motivation is the rest of the way as it apparently will not push overly hard to try and earn the NL's No. 2 seed and that first-round bye.
Atlanta outfielder Mike Yastrzemski is not having a good first year with the Braves, hitting .228 with 10 homers and a slugging percentage of .377. He has slipped into a platoon role, pretty much only starting against right-handers as a lefty hitter; all 10 homers are against right-handers.
But Yastrzemski homered Monday to snap a power drought (23 games) and is 4-for-10 career with a double, triple and homer (1.000 slugging) in his career off Houston starting pitcher Peter Lambert (8-9, 3.71 ERA). The righty has surrendered 14 dingers.
